items.body:
Ministry
: A principal division of a government, often responsible for a specific area like defense or foreign affairs.
Agency
: A government body or organization that performs a particular service, such as intelligence gathering or export control.
National Security Council
: A high-level governmental forum for coordinating national security policy and inter-agency efforts.
Civil Protection Body
: An organization responsible for coordinating efforts to safeguard the population from disasters and emergencies. | Ministry

items.instruction: Match the correct ending to the beginning of these sentences.
items.title: Classify that!
items.body:
Although the phrase 'medical device' may conjure images of intensive care units	
the truth is that many of the products you use every day are also considered medical devices by regulatory bodies.

Toothbrushes, bandages, and latex gloves	
are all examples of low-risk medical devices.

Pregnancy tests, powered wheelchairs, and contact lenses on the other hand	
are considered intermediate-risk devices and are subject to more regulatory controls.

Implants like pacemakers and artificial joints, and life-sustaining equipment like high-frequency ventilators	
are clearly more critical and are classified as high-risk.

Each regulatory authority has different criteria and regulations	
so classifications of specific devices vary around the world.

items.body: Yesterday, Tom and Allison went to the market. Tom wanted to buy some vegetables and Allison needed to buy some cheese. The problems started at the fruit and vegetable stand. Tom picked up a tomato and all the other tomatoes rolled off the table. Then Allison dropped a watermelon and it almost fell on Tom's foot. When they paid for their fruit and vegetables, the owners of the stand gave Tom a sack of potatoes, but the sack broke and all the potatoes fell out. At the cheese stand, Allison dropped her bag on the table and smashed some crackers and then Tom tripped and fell. They decided not to go to the market again.

items.title: What a day!
items.body: Last Monday was the worst day of my life! You know I got a part in a film, right? Well, I was learning my lines when the doorbell rang. It was my neighbor. She was crying like a baby. Well, I invited her in. I mean, what else could I do? While I was making her tea, her friend arrived. And after about a minute, they were shouting at each other. 'You stole my part!' she screamed. 'I didn't get the part either,' my neighbor yelled back. Then the friend began to quote some lines. 'Where were you when our father was dying?' I froze and looked down at the script in my hand. 'I was crying my eyes out,' I whispered.

items.title: 10 principles
items.body:
unobtrusive
	Like tools, products should fulfill a purpose. Good design should be neutral and restrained.

long-lasting
	It avoids fashion and therefore never appears out-of-date.

honest
	Good design doesn't pretend to be more innovative or powerful than it really is.

innovative
	Good design always develops in tandem with technology, and can never be an end in itself.

thorough
	Nothing is arbitrary or left to chance. Good design considers every last detail.

useful
	A product is bought to be used. Good design emphasizes the usefulness of a product and disregards anything that could detract from it.

environmentally friendly
	Good design uses resources responsibly throughout its life cycle.

simple
	Less is more. Good design focuses on the essential.

understandable
	A well-designed product is self-explanatory.

aesthetic
	A well-executed design can be beautiful. Products we use daily affect our person and our well-being. | unobtrusive

then actually experiencing it.

We all view life through a cultural lens	
with its integrated values and norms.

When we meet someone who views things differently,	
our usual approach doesn't work anymore.

Read up on the cultural norms of the country	
you're doing business with beforehand.

Don't generalize, because the person you are with is an individual	
and may find your stereotyping offensive.

items.title: Generation Y
items.body:
Who are the Generation Y'ers and how 
are they changing
 the way we work? Generation Y, born anytime between the late 1970s and 2000, is a new breed. They have been pampered, nurtured and fed on a diet of wide-ranging extracurricular activities.  They've grown up questioning their parents and now 
they're doing
 the same to their employers. Generation Y 
doesn't respond
 well to a command-and-control style of management; they prefer to collaborate. They seek environments where creativity and independent thinking is a prerequisite. Gen Y'ers don't tend to look for one long assignment; they want change. This is a generation of multitaskers; they juggle email on their tablets while chatting on smartphones.  And they 
feel
 completely at home in a virtual world.
Generation Y'ers are not just independent and technically savvy, they 
belong
 to a post-9-11 era. They 
want
 a life and they want their jobs to fit into this picture. They demand flexibility, telecommuting options and the possibility to go part-time – or leave the workforce temporarily – when children are in the picture.  And they 
see
 the full financial picture. Half of all Gen Y'ers 
factor in
 a company's retirement benefits package into their job choices. | are they changing

20th century corporate structures focused on 
vertical
 organization. A large corporation's organization chart would typically show several 
tiers
 of managers, with decision-making 
flow
 moving from top to bottom. This model emphasized job 
specialization
, formal procedures and protocols, and it 
centralized
 authority and accountability.

flat
 hierarchies. In some companies, this has involved extracting several layers of 
middle
 management. The effect was positive.  The 
streamlined
 organization not only saved on personnel costs, but improved communication and decision making.

inclusive
. Some companies institute 
self-directed
 work teams as the standard production group. The move aims to de-emphasize job specialization and 
authority
 and facilitate decision making and goal setting at all levels. | vertical

items.title: Monitoring employee activity
items.body:
More than one-third of the American workforce expects their employer to 
monitor
 their email or even to put them under surveillance on a regular basis. Whether it's gauging employee 
productivity
, complying with 
legal requirements
, ensuring 
data security
 or even fighting corporate 
spying
, companies walk a fine line in the world of workplace 
ethics
.
Where should employers – and employees – draw the line?  Subjecting employees to constant scrutiny may keep the majority on track and catch any 
wrongdoers
, but doing so raises a lot of questions about 
privacy
. Who owns a picture of the family saved on the computer desktop? Is it okay to make personal phone calls during work hours?
The key for company managers is to 
formulate
 a clear policy and make sure employees have not only read it but understood it. Making sure the policy is in keeping with the corporate culture is important, too. A company specializing in web products with a relaxed working environment that suddenly forbids private email usage might have trouble enforcing a strict internet policy. A law firm, which by design is a more conservative workplace, might not.  In any case, if the 
policy
 makes sense, most employees will willingly follow it. | monitor

The dispute, which has been simmering  years, is coming to a boil at a difficult time for Indian movies. items.title: Future famine?
items.body:
In 1968, when the world's population was around 3.7 billion, the American Assembly met to talk about what could be done to head off a potential 
global food
 crisis by the year 2000. The expectation was that the population would double by the millennium.  The number of 
malnourished
 people – estimated to affect about 37 percent of the world's 
population
 in 1970 – was expected to rise as well.
How could governments and global agencies best assist the starving and avoid 
famine
? The Assembly concluded that the US should increase foreign aid and that developing countries should expand birth control measures.  It also recommended encouraging investment by private corporations specializing in 
agricultural
 products and 
food processing
.
Today, the global population is believed to have reached 7 billion.  While the percentage of the population that is 
starving
 has dropped since the 1970s to about 13 percent, rates remain distressingly high. Even with monetary aid and improved crop 
yields
, which are attributed to better 
seed
 stock and farming equipment, an estimated 925 million people still don't get enough to eat. Conversely, in the United States alone, 62 percent of the adult population is 
overweight
 or 
obese
, a number that has doubled since 1970.
Now scientists and organizations are beginning to consider how the world will cope with the estimated 10 billion who may be living on our planet by the year 2100.  How can we make farming more 
sustainable
 and effective? Did any of the measures proposed in 1970 actually help curb hunger? What new methods are available to us now? What new possibilities might work in the future? | global food

items.title: Feedback form
items.body:
'I called up Laptop World when I spilled coffee on my keyboard. I would describe the service I got there as being moderately competent. The customer service representative was quite pleasant, and even patient, but he had to ask for help to solve the problem. When he did give me a response, I have to say that I didn't have any confidence in it. I don't think I would return to Laptop World again.' Janet Doe
'I'm not the type to go off in a tizzy over unenthusiastic customer service. I try to be a little understanding, too. After all, it can't be easy listening to people's problems and complaints every day for 8 hours. I don't think it's right to be too strict with the person. Instead, I try to direct my aggression to the item in question; in my case, that was my laptop which I spilled coffee over. The service rep did his best to reply, though frankly, I had the feeling he was a little unsure. He might have been new. Anyway, would I buy a laptop there again? Yeah, I mean, if I hadn't knocked over my cup, I wouldn't be talking to you right now.' Jasmin Doe
'I was infuriated by the treatment I received when I called Laptop World. The customer service representative was anything but knowledgeable. And professionalism seemed to have gone out of fashion there, too. I was left hanging on the line for ages and when the representative did eventually take my call, he just blurted out the first inane response that came into his head. I told him that I had spilled coffee on my laptop, and before I could finish my sentence, he insisted I get the hairdryer out and dry it. What I tried to tell him – unsuccessfully – was that the incident had happened a week before and that now a couple of the keys didn't work. But, he was too impatient to get me off the line to allow me to explain that. Never again, I say! Never again.' Jane Doe

traits
, such as increased 
yield

susceptibility
 to disease. Although there is concern that crops could cross-pollinate or cause other unexpected health problems to consumers, the percentage of GM crops increases each year.
The success of modified grains has led to further 
experiments on
 other crops, such as potatoes, as well as speculation that 
livestock
 could also be altered to better suit the needs of the market and the environment. Scientists are working hard to develop genetically modified salmon that reach 
market size
 faster or pigs that naturally produce reduced levels of 
greenhouse gases
.
Despite the advances, governments are finding that legalizing genetically modified food is not simple: governments face many challenges in the areas of testing, 
labeling
 and regulation of such products. While many people think 
genetic engineering
 is inevitable, and that we cannot afford to ignore genetically modified food as an 
alternative
 to more traditional methods of food production, others believe we must proceed with 
caution
 to avoid unintentional harm to other life forms. | Genetically modified organisms

items.body:

it was clear that Hollywood

are suffering

items.title: Mergers, mergers
items.body:
merger
	the marriage between two or more companies in the same industry to form one organization

hostile takeover
	the acquisition of a company, whose management doesn't want the takeover, but which happens regardless

horizontal merger
	a merger between companies that are in direct competition and share the same product lines and markets

market-extension merger
	the merger of companies that sell the same products in different markets

product-extension merger
	the merger of companies selling different but related products in the same market

conglomeration
	a marriage of companies that have no common business areas

merger of equals
	a merger between companies of the same size and interests

vertical merger
	a merger between a customer and company, or between a supplier and manufacturer, like a food packaging supplier merging with a frozen pizza manufacturer

items.body:
In an ultra-competitive world, having a mature network of supply-chain partners can give a business an edge and over its competitors. However, there are relatively few tools to help managers but calculate the development levels of their supply chains.
In the supply-chain context, Done defines a 'mature' company as one such that cooperates across a wide range of partners to establish the kind of practices that of lead to greater coordination. 'Immature' companies, on the other hand, engage less, furthermore using a limited number of supply-chain partners and a narrower range of supply-chain-integration practices.
To capture in addition to the multidimensional nature of supply-chain activity, Done bases his evaluation of maturity on six key areas of operations are: planning, sourcing, manufacturing, delivery, new-product development and returns.

With 5G, gamers can enjoy smoother gameplay, quicker response times, and the ability to connect multiple devices without significant lag, thus revolutionizing how games are paid and experienced. These advancements not only enhance the user experience but also drive higher data usage, as more gamers can participate in data-intensive activities spontaneously.
The symbiotic relationship between online gaming and telecoms continues to involve, with both industries pushing the boundaries of technology and data consumption. Telecom companies are increasingly collaborating with game developers and platforms to optimize data delivery and enhance user experiments. Innovations such as hedgehog computing, which processes data closer to the end-user, are being implemented to reduce latency and improve performance. As online gaming continues to grow in popularity, the ongoing development and adaptation of telecom structure will be crucial in supporting the data-heavy demands of this dynamic and rapidly changing sector.

items.title: Healthcare systems
items.body:
The Beveridge Model	
A single-payer healthcare system in which the majority of the hospitals and doctors work for the government

The Bismarck Model	
A single-payer healthcare system where health care is provided through insurance companies who are paid by employer and employee payroll deductions

The National Health Insurance Model	
Healthcare is paid through higher taxation, though patients are free to choose any doctor or hospital they wish

The Private Insurance System	
In this system, individuals are either covered by their employers or private insurance policies they purchase themselves, or they go without any coverage.

items.title: Re-engagement strategies
items.body:
While there are 
myriad
 reasons why employees become disengaged from their work, there are several common causes, and thus, several common solutions that can be adapted to the particular situation. A typical source of 
discontent
 is a lack of transparency regarding the company's mission and goals. This can be addressed by improving communication between management and employees. The way of doing this can be adapted to the particular needs and culture of the company, but could be as simple as creating a regular newsletter to update employees on the goals and mission of the company or as complex as creating an online platform where all the workers in the company can 
interact
 and exchange ideas and information about projects, progress, and targets.
Disengaged employees often feel that their careers are 
stagnant
 and see few possibilities for growth and development. This problem can be tackled in numerous ways, from developing mentoring programs wherein managers can help employees to discover potential directions for their careers, to dedicating time during performance 
appraisals
 to identify what employees want their next steps to be, to being more 
proactive
 about promoting lateral moves within the company.
Other reasons for disengagement call less for an 
overhaul
 of a company's processes than changes in the behavior of certain managers. Many employees say that micromanagement of their tasks causes them to become disengaged, so managers should evaluate their ways of doing things and consider offering their 
reports
 greater flexibility and autonomy to complete their tasks as they see fit. Managers should also take the time to say thank you to their subordinates for a job well done, as disengaged employees often report feeling taken 
for granted
, with their managers failing to show any appreciation or acknowledgement of their hard work. In some cases, a few small 
tweaks
 to the way managers deal with their employees are all that are needed to bring disengaged workers back into the fold. | myriad

items.title: The very basics
items.body:
A solvent is a substance used to dissolve, extract, or clean materials in industries such as pharmaceuticals, paints, and metal processing.
An acid is a chemical that donates hydrogen ions and is commonly used in metal treatment, battery production, and chemical synthesis.
An alkali is a basic substance that neutralizes acids and is widely used in cleaning products, water treatment, and paper manufacturing.
Fertilizers are chemical products added to soil to supply essential nutrients and improve crop growth in agriculture.
Pesticides are substances used in farming and public health to control insects, weeds, fungi, and other harmful organisms.
Neutralization is a reaction between an acid and an alkali that is used in wastewater treatment and chemical processing to control pH levels.
A solvent extraction process uses a solvent to separate valuable compounds from raw materials, for example in metal refining or pharmaceutical production.
Corrosive substances are chemicals that can damage materials or skin and are commonly handled with special storage and safety procedures in manufacturing plants.
Dilution is the process of reducing concentration by adding a solvent, often done in laboratories and industrial production to reach required purity or strength levels.

Corrosive substances are chemicals that can damage materials or skin and are commonly handled with special storage and safety procedures in manufacturing plants.
Dilution is the process of reducing concentration by adding a solvent, often done in laboratories and industrial production to reach required purity or strength levels.

items.title: Behind the scenes: Chemicals at work
items.body:
Industrial production relies on a wide range of basic chemicals that serve as essential inputs in many processes. Acids are used in metal treatment, mineral processing, and battery manufacturing, while alkalis are important for cleaning operations and water treatment. Solutions are widely applied in pharmaceuticals, coats, and extraction processes, where they dissolve or separate substances. Maintaining the correct reconcentration and purity of these chemicals is essential for consistent product quality.
In industrial settings, chemical strength is often adjusted through delusion or neutralization to control pH and reaction conditions. Many of these instances have hazardous properties such as flammability, volatility, or corrosiveness, so proper store and material compatibility are critical. Poor handling can lead to contamination of products or corrosion of equipment.
Fertilizers and pesticides are major chemical product groups used in agriculture to improve crop yields and protect ants. They require careful formulation and accurate concentration to ensure both effectiveness and safety. Even small variations in composition can effect performance or create environmental concerns.
Across industries, chemicals act as feedstocks, intermediates, and reagents in complex production chains. Strict quality control helps prevent insecurities from affecting downstream products, while proper storage, labeling, and disposal support safe operations and regulatory complication.

items.instruction: Match the correct ending to the beginning of these sentences.
items.title: Who uses CCS?
items.body:
Coal and natural gas power plants use
	post-combustion carbon capture to reduce emissions before releasing flue gases into the atmosphere.

The cement industry captures CO2 from kilns,
	where limestone decomposition releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.

Steel plants integrate CCS by
	capturing CO2 from blast furnaces and storing it in geological formations.

Fossil fuel companies use captured CO2 for enhanced oil recovery,
	injecting it into reservoirs to extract more crude oil while storing some carbon underground.

Ammonia and hydrogen production facilities apply CCS
	to reduce emissions from reforming and gasification processes.

Some pulp mills capture CO2 from biomass combustion,
